observation_summary: The method StringUtils.containsIgnoreCase fails in certain locales because it uses locale-sensitive case conversion (String.toUpperCase/toLowerCase), which is inappropriate for general case-insensitive string comparisons.
reasoning_summary: The bug report explicitly identifies that the use of locale-sensitive case conversion is the root cause of the failure. This is a classic algorithmic error where the implementation of a case-insensitive comparison method uses an incorrect procedure (locale-dependent conversion) instead of a locale-independent one. This fits the ODC definition of an Algorithm/Method defect, as it involves correcting the logic/procedure used to perform the comparison.
evidence_used: bug_report_description: String.to*Case() is locale-sensitive, this is usually not intended for case-insensitive comparisions.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix does not require a design change or a new capability; it is a local correction to the logic of an existing method.
The issue is not a missing or incorrect validation check, but rather the use of an incorrect transformation algorithm within the method.
